title: Canonical integral completion as a strict presentation
statement:
Fix a prime l, a finite field extension E/Q_l and a scheme X with the project size convention. For the actual condensed integer ring and its pulled-back module category, there exists a strict scalar-cone completion presentation S [def-sfb-strict-completion-restriction-data] satisfying IsIntegral l E X S. In particular the datum is canonical, its scalar is the pulled-back uniformizer, its tower and augmentations are the specified principal cones, its reductions and transitions are the actual derived coefficient changes, and its completion/unit is the specified augmented completion.

Exact Lean assertion:
theorem strictIntegralCompletionPresentation (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    ∃ S : Presentation.{u + 2, u + 1, u + 1} (AdicCompletion.Modules l E X),
      IsIntegral l E X S

proof.text:
Extract the canonical cone datum and its coordinate, transition, augmentation
and localization equalities from completion_triangle_comparison. Express the scalar
of the datum as an endomorphism of the identity functor. Functoriality and cancellation
of the regular-module comparison identify its powers with the given cone powers.
Use the canonical scalar-extension adjunction to assemble the reduction transitions
as natural transformations. The supplied descent equalities give every reduction
field. The completion and its unit are precisely those of the input theorem.
